entries.n: From Latin; the Biblical use matches the Latin original and survives in 'acceptable'.

entries.m: worthy of acceptance or approval; then agreeable, delightful
entries.n: Used like the Latin original; in the New Testament it often stands for the Greek word elsewhere rendered 'well-pleasing'.

entries.m: to complete, make complete; used of number or time
entries.n: The word had a wider use formerly. We speak of accomplishing a task, but not a number or period of time.

entries.m: acquaintances, used as a collective noun
